task: Silage Surface Visual Anomaly & Mould-like Screening

class_definitions.NO_MOLD: Normal fermented silage appearance: chopped whole-crop maize/grass/sorghum forage, compacted bunker clamp face, or baled forage displaying typical fermentation color (olive-green to golden-brown) without visible superficial fungal hyphae or sporulating mycelial colonies.
class_definitions.VISIBLE_MOLD: Silage or forage surface exhibiting visible fungal mycelium, filamentous mold colonies, white/grey/green/black sporulation patches, or overt aerobic spoilage deterioration.

multimodal_mapping.mouldProbability: Probability assigned to class VISIBLE_MOLD by the vision model softmax output.
multimodal_mapping.visual_safety_score: Continuous score 0-100 calculated as (1.0 - mouldProbability) * 100 for integration into the Multimodal Screening Score Index (MSSI).
multimodal_mapping.rule_engine_integration: If mouldProbability >= 0.70, triggers screening ALERT. If mouldProbability >= 0.40, triggers screening CAUTION/BORDERLINE.

scientific_disclaimer: CRITICAL: Visible mould is a qualitative visual screening signal. It DOES NOT quantify biochemical mycotoxin concentration (aflatoxin B1, deoxynivalenol, zearalenone) in parts per billion (ppb). Laboratory HPLC/ELISA analysis is required for analytical toxin quantification.
